model.name: Boot must be READ-MOSTLY and CORPUS-INDEPENDENT — bootstrapSeed's O(all-units) scan is a latent outage (delete it; seed lazily at point-of-use)
model.description: MEASURED CAUSE (two independent angles CONVERGED — expert empirically + architect from code, ruling 451c47e64): FeatureManager.bootstrapSeed is a SYNCHRONOUS, ZERO-YIELD loop that calls ScenarioIndex.get for EVERY uuid (~5677) — and get is a readFileSync+JSON.parse with NO cache — merely to filter a handful of Features. So /api/config CANNOT answer until the entire corpus is scanned: a pure O(corpus) stall present even SOLO (not contention). It is a LATENT OUTAGE THAT WORSENS DAILY with no code change (the corpus only grows). Boot must be READ-MOSTLY and CORPUS-INDEPENDENT: O(1) or O(features), never O(all-units); the preferred shape seeds features LAZILY at point-of-use (the auth path already loads allowedUsers) so boot does ZERO corpus work.

One bad shape, two faces.

acceptanceCriteria.text: Boot work is INDEPENDENT of corpus size — O(1) or O(features), NEVER O(all-units). DELETE the bootstrapSeed idx.get-every-unit scan; /api/config must answer without scanning the corpus. Provable: boot get-call-count does NOT grow with total-unit-count.

PREFERRED shape: seed-if-absent LAZILY at point-of-use (the auth path already loads allowedUsers) so boot does ZERO corpus work. ACCEPTABLE alternatives: (a) boot as a read-only ASSERT with an EXPLICIT repair path (no silent mutation at boot); (b) FALLBACK — O(features)-via-type-index + ONE ATOMIC write (temp+rename) + a YIELDING loop. NEVER the synchronous zero-yield O(all-units) loop.

A GATE FAILS if boot touches every unit: instrument the ScenarioIndex.get-call-count AND a boot completion-time BUDGET; STUB-MUST-FAIL — plant a corpus scan at boot and assert the gate goes RED. A boot that re-grows to O(corpus) is caught by construction, not by the next outage.

Close the NON-ATOMIC whole-file read-modify-write on Feature writes: a concurrent boot can tear / lost-update the Feature file (same class as the token-reembed trap). Feature persistence uses an atomic write (temp+rename) so a concurrent reader never sees a torn file and no update is lost.
